messages.subject: Variable number of inputs
parts:
Simply put, my goal is to have the UI have a variable number of inputs (input$var1, input$var2, ..., input$varN), based on how many columns the respective annotation has.  If there are 2 columns, 2 groups of check boxes would appear to select from, if there are 12 columns, 12 groups of check boxes appear, etc.  Conditional panels at a glance would work, but require manually writing out a panel up to the potential maximum number of columns- it would probably end up being tedious should larger annotation files come into play.

The best short example of what I am after would actually be Reactivity in the tutorial- rock has a different number of columns than pressure.  If we wanted to have distinct clusters of check boxes populated by respective columns for the given data set, is this outside the current capabilities of shiny?

Thanks again for your time and attention,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Variable number of inputs
parts:
That actually isn't quite what I had in mind.  I am able to manipulate a single variable field at this point, my question is being able to create multiple fields and use their distinct inputs.

Suppose in one dataset, there are 3 columns to the annotation, HPV status (positive, negative), Cancer status (Tumor, Normal), and Stage (0,1,2,3,4), and the other dataset has 2 columns to the annotation, Subsite (lung, breast, colon, etc), Recurrence (positive, negative).  Selecting the first data set would create 3 input fields

HPV status
o positive
o negative

Cancer status
o Tumor
o Normal

Stage
o 0
o 1
o 2
o 3
o 4

while the other would produce:

Subsite
o lung
o breast
o colon
o other

Recurrence
o positive
o negative

Currently, I am capable of producing a single input field filled with the union of all of the potential selections (ie positive, negative, tumor, normal, 1, 2, 3, 4).  However, this is potentially troublesome when looking at how the data sets will be selected. If there is only one input field, either the union or intersection of the selected fields would be possible, however it is easy to imagine a situation where someone wanted to select one group of Tumors (all HPV status, all Stages) and one group of Normals (all HPV status, all Stages)- taking the union of all matches would yield every sample in each of the two groups (all samples are either HPV positive or negative), while taking the intersect would result in the two groups being empty (no sample can be both HPV positive and HPV negative).  As such, I need a way to organize it to be the union of the selected within columns, and intersect between them, to subset the data.  Does this clarify what I am after?

Thanks!
Mike

Hello Mike,

I had the same problem. I solved it by defining two storage classes of the data

setClass("CancerStorage",
         representation(sName    = "character", # name of the cancer
                        dtData   = "data.table", # the data
                        lProfile = "CancerProfile", # the information for building the ui for this data set
                             )
         )

and

setClass("OCDMProfile",
         representation(cShinyClass = "character", # a character vector of the shiny inputs, e.g. slider, numeric, select, dependent on 
                        cInputID    = "character", #  a character vector for the InputIDs
                        cLabel      = "character", #  a character vector of the Labels
                        lChoices    = "list"),     # List of character vector for the choices, if they exist, else there must be a placeholder
         )

I load the data into this storages classe and save it into a subdir data. When the App starts-up, my App looks into this dir and build a selectInput with the type of cancer data from the dir of data. If the user selects one he gets the profile to select from the storage class. I hope the idea helps you. 

Simon

messages.subject: Re: Variable number of inputs
parts:
I send you my two functions for this task:

The first function is for getting one ui element and the second one puts them together. The iProfile variable is used for comparing the same dataset on different selection, e.g. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

#' Create a ui element for the profile
#'
#' This function builds an ui element, e.g. slider, numerics for the profile
#'
#' @param object The CancerStorage class
#' @param iPObjekt The integer number of the object to build
#' @param iProfil The profile ID
#'
#' @return a ui element
#'
#' @export
getProfileObject <- function(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=1) { 
  
  if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "slider") {
    
    # sliderInput
    rn <- range(object@dtData[[object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt]]])
    sliderInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""),
                label   = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt],
                min     = rn[1],
                max     = rn[2],
                value   = c(rn[1], rn[2]),
                step    = 1,
                format  = "####")
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "select") {
    
    # selectInput
    selectInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""), 
          label         = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt], 
          choices       = object@lProfile@lChoices[[iPObjekt]] )
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "numeric") {
    
    # numericInput
  
  } else {
    
  }
  
}

#' Create the profile UI
#'
#' This function builds the ui wih the sliders, inputs etc. profile for the 
#' user interaction
#' 
#' @param object The CancerStorage -Class
#' @param ... Tnput variables 
#'
#' @return A sidebar ui panel of the profile
#'
#' @export
buildProfileUI <- function(object, iProfile=1) {
  
  m <- length(object@lProfile@cInputID)
  lP <- list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=iProfile), br())
  for (i in 2:(m-1)) {
    lP <- c(lP, 
            list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=i, iProfil=iProfile)), 
            list(br()))
  }
  lP <- c(lP, list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=m, iProfil=iProfile)))
  lP
  
}

you get then something like this. Until now I was not able to publish my App, since my tools is not finished yet and the data is sensitive.

Simon

I haven't looked closely enough at Simon's solution to comment on it, but to me this sounds like a job for renderUI. Winston's example only produced a single checkboxGroupInput, but renderUI can return arbitrarily many inputs (and outputs if so desired).

To consume inputs dynamically (i.e. if you can't write input$foo because you don't know what "foo" is going to be) you can use input[["foo"]] (I believe that works) or `$`(input, "foo") (this definitely works).

If that's not enough to get you going, let us know. Sorry, I'm in a rush right now.

#' Create a ui element for the profile
#'
#' This function builds an ui element, e.g. slider, numerics for the profile

#' @param iPObjekt The integer number of the object to build
#' @param iProfil The profile ID
#'
#' @return a ui element
#'
#' @export
getProfileObject <- function(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=1) { 
  
  if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "slider") {
    
    # sliderInput
    rn <- range(object@dtData[[object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt]]])
    sliderInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""),
                label   = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt],
                min     = rn[1],
                max     = rn[2],
                value   = c(rn[1], rn[2]),
                step    = 1,
                format  = "####")
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "select") {
    
    # selectInput
    selectInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""), 
          label         = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt], 
          choices       = object@lProfile@lChoices[[iPObjekt]] )
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "numeric") {
    
    # numericInput
  
  } else {
    
  }
  
}

#' Create the profile UI
#'
#' This function builds the ui wih the sliders, inputs etc. profile for the 
#' user interaction
#' 
#' @param object The CancerStorage -Class
#' @param ... Tnput variables 
#'
#' @return A sidebar ui panel of the profile
#'
#' @export
buildProfileUI <- function(object, iProfile=1) {
  
  m <- length(object@lProfile@cInputID)
  lP <- list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=iProfile), br())
  for (i in 2:(m-1)) {
    lP <- c(lP, 
            list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=i, iProfil=iProfile)), 
            list(br()))
  }
  lP <- c(lP, list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=m, iProfil=iProfile)))
  lP
  
}

checkboxGroupInput returns the HTML for that control. (The same is true for any of the other input/output functions you use in ui.R.) In your "for" loop, you're creating the HTML and then dropping it on the floor. You just need to collect them in a list and return it, then it should work.

output$subsetControl <- renderUI({
  lapply(1:ncol(datasetInput()), function(i) {
    subss <-    unique(datasetInput()[,i])
    checkboxGroupInput(paste("subsst",i,sep=""), colnames(datasetInput())[i], choices=subss, selected=subss)
  })
})

I send you my two functions for this task:

The first function is for getting one ui element and the second one puts them together. The iProfile variable is used for comparing the same dataset on different selection, e.g. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

#' Create a ui element for the profile
#'
#' This function builds an ui element, e.g. slider, numerics for the profile
#'
#' @param object The CancerStorage class
#' @param iPObjekt The integer number of the object to build
#' @param iProfil The profile ID
#'
#' @return a ui element
#'
#' @export
getProfileObject <- function(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=1) { 
  
  if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "slider") {
    
    # sliderInput
    rn <- range(object@dtData[[object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt]]])
    sliderInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""),
                label   = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt],
                min     = rn[1],
                max     = rn[2],
                value   = c(rn[1], rn[2]),
                step    = 1,
                format  = "####")
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "select") {
    
    # selectInput
    selectInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""), 
          label         = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt], 
          choices       = object@lProfile@lChoices[[iPObjekt]] )
    
  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "numeric") {
    
    # numericInput
  
  } else {
    
  }
  
}

#' Create the profile UI
#'
#' This function builds the ui wih the sliders, inputs etc. profile for the 
#' user interaction
#' 
#' @param object The CancerStorage -Class
#' @param ... Tnput variables 
#'
#' @return A sidebar ui panel of the profile
#'
#' @export
buildProfileUI <- function(object, iProfile=1) {
  
  m <- length(object@lProfile@cInputID)
  lP <- list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=iProfile), br())
  for (i in 2:(m-1)) {
    lP <- c(lP, 
            list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=i, iProfil=iProfile)), 
            list(br()))
  }
  lP <- c(lP, list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=m, iProfil=iProfile)))
  lP
  
}

Excellent- thank you.  I waited to respond until I had a working way of subsetting the data by rows selected.  I am including the code I used in case it will be useful to those who come to this thread with similar questions:

(relevant code only)


output$choose_columns <- renderUI({ # this is the code taken from the column subsetting example ...to subset columns
# If missing input, return to avoid error later in function
if(is.null(input$dataset))
return()
 
# Get the data set with the appropriate name
dat <- get(input$dataset)
colnames <- names(dat)
 
# Create the checkboxes and select them all by default
checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns",
choices = colnames,
selected = colnames)
})
 


anno1 <-    reactive({ # this is to subset the data to the columns selected
if(is.null(input$dataset))
return()

dat <- get(input$dataset)
 
if (is.null(input$columns) || !(input$columns %in% names(dat)))
return()



dat <- dat[, input$columns, drop = FALSE]
 })

output$subsetControl1 <- renderUI({ # this code is to implement the various number of checkbox groups
 
  lapply(1:ncol(anno1()), function(i) {

    subss <-    unique(anno1()[,i])
    checkboxGroupInput(paste("
subssta",i,sep=""), colnames(anno1())[i], choices=subss, selected=subss)
  })
})


 anno1b=reactive({ # this is to subset the data to the rows which have a selected data type
 if(is.null(input$dataset))
return()

 dat <- get(input$dataset)
 
 if (is.null(input$columns) || !(input$columns %in% names(dat)))
return()


 subs=rownames(dat)

 for(i in 1:length(input$columns)){
 colx=input$columns[i]
 subx1=dat[,colx]%in%input[[paste("subssta",i,sep="")]]
 subx2=rownames(dat[subx1,])
 subs=intersect(subs,subx2)

 }
    anno1()[subs,]
